chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Amr ibn Ilyas, who said:

I performed Hajj with my father while I was a Sarurah (one who has not yet performed Hajj). So I said, 'I would like to make my Hajj on behalf of my mother, for she has died.' He said to me, 'Wait until I ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for you.' So Ilyas said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was listening, 'May I be your sacrifice! This son of mine is a Sarurah, and his mother has died, so he would like to make his mother has died, so he would like to make his Hajj for her. Is that permissible for him?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is written for him and for her, and it is written for him the reward of righteousness.'

key_terms.أَجْرُ الْبِرِّ: The reward of righteousness or filial piety
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: A person who has not yet performed their obligatory Hajj
key_terms.يُكْتَبُ لَهُ وَ لَهَا: It is recorded/written for him and for her (indicating shared validity)

ai.seo_question: Can a son perform Hajj on behalf of his deceased mother if he has not yet performed his own obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a 'Sarurah' (one who has not yet performed their obligatory Hajj) may perform Hajj on behalf of a deceased parent, with the reward shared between the deceased and the performer. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifically highlights that the son receives the distinct reward of 'al-birr' (filial piety), emphasizing the spiritual merit of fulfilling parental duties even after death. This ruling underscores the Shia view that Hajj is a transferable obligation, allowing living descendants to complete the religious duty for those who passed away without fulfilling it.
